analysis.investment_thesis: Clean Science has an enviable quality profile — zero debt, 27% ROCE, and 62% gross margins in niche specialty chemicals — but the current price at 20.4x EV/EBITDA and a FCF yield of just 0.9% (INR 72 Cr FCF / INR 8,052 Cr market cap) leaves virtually no margin of safety. After peaking in FY2023, both EBITDA and net profit have essentially flat-lined for three years, yet the market continues to price in perfection.
key_strengths: Zero debt balance sheet with 27.3% ROCE and 61.95% gross margins — exceptional capital efficiency reflecting real pricing power in niche performance chemicals (MEHQ, BHA, TBHQ)
Proven 7-year track record: revenue CAGR of 22%, net profit CAGR of 27.2% — genuine compounding through disciplined operations
Consistent OCF positivity (5/5 years) and near-zero finance costs signal a management culture of financial conservatism
key_risks: Growth has materially stalled — EBITDA ranged only INR 346–420 Cr over FY2023–FY2025, essentially flat for three years despite a premium valuation of 32.8x P/E
Specialty chemicals cyclicality is real: revenue fell 15% in FY2024 (936 → 791 Cr) due to China pricing pressure and global demand softness; the cycle can repeat
Rising capex (INR 232 Cr in FY2024, INR 142 Cr in FY2025) against flat EBITDA means return on incremental investment is unproven; CWIP at INR 98 Cr is growing
red_flags: FCF yield of only ~0.9% (INR 72 Cr / INR 8,052 Cr MCap) — investors are paying far ahead of current cash generation
Other income of INR 39 Cr represents ~15% of net profit — treasury/investment income propping up headline earnings
Revenue declined from INR 936 Cr (FY2023) to INR 791 Cr (FY2024), confirming the business is not recession-proof despite its quality narrative
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Clean Science is genuinely a high-quality business — zero debt, 27% ROCE, and 62% gross margins in specialty chemicals are not easily replicated. The 7-year profit CAGR of 27.2% is evidence of real value creation. But second-level thinking demands we ask: what does the price already reflect? At 20.4x EV/EBITDA and 32.8x P/E, the market is paying for a compounding machine. The problem is that the compounding appears to have paused — EBITDA peaked at INR 420 Cr in FY2023 and remains below that peak at INR 399 Cr in FY2025.

The FCF story is the most sobering data point: INR 72 Cr of free cash flow against an INR 8,052 Cr market cap is a 0.9% yield — you are not being compensated for risk. The specialty chemicals cycle exposed the vulnerability (FY2024 revenue down 15%), and the new capex being deployed (INR 232 Cr in FY2024 alone) hasn't yet translated into earnings growth. The business deserves a premium, but not one that prices in acceleration that isn't happening. Fair value, not a bargain.
